Interpretation: the parity-breaking token is consistent with a row-wise verify hidden-state defect rather than a pure commit-slot misread; the defective site is NOT identified.

learning: New bounded packet-level result: NGRAM ON's parity-breaking token is not a commit that contradicts the row it reports (own argmax, gap 0, 4/4), and the verifier's reported distribution at the same visible prefix is itself materially different from the bit-exact reproducible OFF distribution (1/4 case far beyond a near-tie; 3/4 near-ties within ON's own row). This shifts the weight from 'commit reads the wrong slot' toward row-wise verify hidden-state/mask/position assembly (candidate A), and adds a concrete structural clue: position 3 carries a systematic ON-vs-OFF LP offset in all 10 pairs while the median matched position is within 0.009 nat. It does not identify the defective site, does not exclude post-commit KV pollution of later steps, and does not close any root/mask/overlap/mover path. Limits: 4 replay cases / 3 unique prefixes, top-8 only, reported LPs not recomputed logits, trace-free, ON/OFF batch compositions differ, replay probes max_tokens=1, no accept_len=1 control. F1 remains BUG_CONFIRMED; no promotion, numeric, speed or gate claim.
